en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Chattupāhanavagga 89.
The Training Rule on Perfumed Footwear.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs bathed with scented oil-cakes.
People complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
"How can these bhikkhunīs bathe with scented oil-cakes? They are just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures!"
The bhikkhunīs heard those people grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [and so forth]... they grumbled, complained, and criticized:
"How can the bhikkhunīs of the group of six bathe with scented sesamum paste?"... [and so forth]...
“Is it true, monks, that the group-of-six bhikkhunīs bathe with scented mustard-paste?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
"How indeed, monks, could the group-of-six bhikkhunīs bathe with scented sesame paste?
This, monks, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of the faith of those who have it...
And furthermore, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule as follows:"
“Whatever nun should bathe with scented sesamum paste, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Regarding “whatever nun”:
whoever she may be... [and so on].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Washed" means:
Whatever is scented with fragrance.
"Piññāka" is said to be sesame flour.
"Should bathe" means she bathes. There is an offense of wrong-doing in the act; at the conclusion of the bathing, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
There is no offense—
On account of illness,
she bathes with ordinary soap;
[this is not an offense] for one who is insane.
"By one who is a first offender.
The sixth training rule is concluded.
